subject: dsa
title: Decode Ways
summary: Like Climbing Stairs over digits: the ways to decode up to a position add the ways from one digit back (if this digit is a valid 1-9 letter) and the ways from two digits back (if the last two digits form 10-26).
problem: A=1, B=2, ..., Z=26. Count how many ways a digit string can be decoded into letters.

steps.caption: Decode '226' with A=1 ... Z=26 and count the ways. Let ways[i] = decodings of the first i digits; ways[0] = 1 for the empty prefix.
First digit '2' is between 1 and 9, a valid single letter (B), so after one digit there is 1 way.
Second digit: '2' alone is valid (+1 way), and '22' is between 10 and 26 (+1 way). Total so far: 2 ways.
Third digit: '6' alone is valid (carry the 2 ways), and '26' is between 10 and 26 (add the 1 way from before the '2 2').
